mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that negates the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation remains below 2% over the signal period, indicating that wage pressures are not spilling over into consumer prices and thus will not trigger a hawkish Fed response.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < -2%), it signals a supply chain disruption that will negatively impact corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX earnings estimates actually rise over the signal period, indicating that the supply shock is not materially impacting corporate profitability.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Real GDP growth accelerates over the next two quarters, indicating that the high interest rates are not slowing the economy as expected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates (3-month change > 10%) and the unemployment rate is low (< 5%), it signals a strong consumer demand environment that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence index falls by more than 10 points over the signal period, indicating that the demand strength may be fleeting.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < 100k) and the unemployment rate is already high (> 6%), it signals a weakening labor market that will slow consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fall by more than 20% over the signal period, indicating that the labor market may be stabilizing rather than weakening further.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is rising and the CPI inflation rate is above 3%, it signals a high-inflation, tightening monetary policy environment that will depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 10-year Treasury yield falls by more than 50 basis points over the signal period, indicating that the bond market is not pricing in persistently high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: When real consumer spending growth accelerates (3-month change > 5%) and industrial production growth is also strong (3-month change > 3%), it signals a broad-based economic expansion that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The ISM manufacturing index falls below 50 over the signal period, indicating that the industrial strength may be reversing.
